title: The Loan Officer and AI — Check

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best use of a general-purpose AI chatbot for a Kapitus loan officer?
choices: Asking it whether a borderline applicant should be approved given their cash-flow profile
Drafting the first version of a follow-up email asking an applicant for a missing bank statement
Looking up Kapitus's current prepayment penalty schedule for a 12-month product
Generating the regulatory citations to include in an adverse action notice
questions.explanation: Drafting outbound communication is the sweet spot — the judgment is already yours, AI just helps you say it faster. The other three are decision-making, product-fact lookup, and regulatory citation, all of which the model will guess at with confidence and frequently get wrong.

questions.prompt: An applicant calls confused about why their offer amount dropped from the pre-qual to the final terms. You know the reason: their bank statements showed more seasonal revenue volatility than the pre-qual assumed. Where does AI fit in this conversation?
choices: Paste the applicant's bank statement into a chatbot and ask it to explain the change to the applicant directly
Ask the chatbot whether the offer should have been reduced, then relay its answer to the applicant
Ask the chatbot to help you phrase 'seasonal revenue volatility caused the reduction' in plain, non-technical language you can use on the call
Skip AI entirely — anything involving an applicant on a live call is off-limits for AI assistance
questions.explanation: The decision is already made and the data is already evaluated. AI's role here is translation — turning 'seasonal revenue volatility' into a sentence the applicant will actually understand. Pasting bank statements is a data exposure, asking the chatbot to second-guess the underwriting decision is outside what the tool can do, and avoiding AI entirely is overcorrection.

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the mental model this lesson recommends?
choices: AI is a junior analyst — give it the data and let it recommend a decision you can override
AI is a search engine — use it to look up Kapitus product terms and regulatory rules
AI is a drafting assistant, never the decision-maker — you decide what to do, AI helps you say it
AI is a compliance reviewer — let it check your work for ECOA violations before sending
questions.explanation: The drafting-assistant framing keeps the human responsible for every decision and uses AI for the genuinely-helpful surface tasks. The other framings put AI in roles it cannot fill: it does not have current Kapitus product data, it is not a regulator, and treating it as a junior analyst encourages exactly the kind of rubber-stamping this lesson warns against.
